About Me

I'm a backend and database-focused software developer with a strong foundation in building scalable server-side architecture, managing relational databases (PostgreSQL). I also have hands-on experience with mobile development using Flutter/Dart, and 3D modeling/visualization tools like Blender.
summary: Mars Survival is a first-person 3D game, built in Unity, in which students keep a Mars research station alive for 12 sols until a rescue crew arrives. Players balance life support (oxygen, CO₂, water and filters), power and heating, food production in a greenhouse, and protection from radiation storms. Every choice shows up in the next sol’s station readings, so students learn the engineering trade-offs that decide a mission’s success by living through them, not by reading about them.
details: Each sol brings 3–4 maintenance tasks, shown on a handheld field terminal. Players service equipment, adjust heating, electrolysis, filtration and recycling on the main terminal, and review the previous sol’s readings to see the effect of their decisions. Food is grown in four greenhouse beds with 20 planting spots: the first crop ripens on sol 4, each plant yields 1 kg of potatoes, a cooked meal restores 50 fullness, and sleeping costs 20. Radiation storm warnings give 20 seconds to get inside and seal the airlock and garage before a 10-second storm. An ice rover collects water ice and returns to base. Finishing sol 12 triggers a rescue cutscene. Team JAMA: Egamov Muhammad (music director), Garayeva Diana (game developer), Sodiqov Abdujalil (3D model artist), Saidjanov Jahongir (map and terrain artist), Abdurrahmon Jurayev (QA). Built with Unity and C#.
dataRefs: Mars terrain: NASA Perseverance rover panoramas and videos of Jezero Crater
Radiation: Curiosity rover Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD) surface measurements, Hassler et al. 2014
